headline: Bond vol ripped to 110 with the whole curve at 52-week highs — and today credit finally started paying the bill.
summary: The long end took another leg: 30y +5bp to 5.64%, 10y +3bp to 5.29%, 5y +3bp to 5.09%, all three at the 100th percentile of the last 52 weeks. The 10y real yield is 2.93%, +49bp on the month with acceleration 1.54, while 5y and 10y breakevens sit inert at 2.36% (+5bp each on the month). That is term premium, not inflation expectations. The violence is in the vol leg: MOVE +3.6% to 110.45, +46.6% on the month, z=2.56, acceleration 1.98 — faster now than yesterday, which is the single most important accelerating series on the board and it is accelerating the wrong way. Rates composite -84. TLT, IEF and LQD all remain pinned at the 0th percentile of their 52-week ranges. The curve is steepening the ugly way: 3m10y 1.09 at the 100th percentile, 2s10s +4bp to 0.41, driven by the back end selling off, not the front end easing (3m bill 4.20%, still +29bp on the month).

What changed today is credit. Yesterday the line was that credit had not paid for any of this. Now HYG is -0.2% on the day, -1.7% on the week, -2.5% on the month, z=-1.57 with acceleration -1.32 and a rolling_over trend; LQD is -3.3% on the month at the 0th percentile. The ratio trade (HYG/IEF, 93.9th percentile) still looks fine because Treasuries are falling as fast as junk — that is cosmetic comfort, not spread discipline. Meanwhile the hedges keep getting cheaper into weaker internals: VIX 16.34 at the 16th percentile, VIX3M 18.37 at the 8th, SKEW -1.8% to 141.92. RSP/SPY printed +0.1% but still sits at the 10th percentile with z=-2.02; IWM/SPY -5.0% on the month; DJT -1.4% today and -9.0% on the month, z=-1.60. Vol priced at the 16th percentile against breadth at the 10th and bond vol at z=2.56 is the cleanest asymmetry on the page.

Under the index (-0.3% to 7,651.5, NDX +0.2%, DJI -0.9%) the barbell got more extreme, not less. Semis did the lifting: SMH +1.1%, SOXX +1.2% and +11.6% on the month, SMH/SPY +1.3% with z=1.34, ASML +3.6%, TSM +0.9% (+9.7% month), MU +1.1%, AMD +30.5% on the month and 64% above its 200-day. META added +3.2% for +27.9% on the month (z=2.24, acceleration 1.85). AAPL gave back -2.7% of yesterday's bounce. Against that, the rate-sensitive and capital-markets complex is in open liquidation: XLF -6.7% on the month with -6.3% relative strength despite record curve steepness, BX -19.9% on the month (z=-2.05, acceleration -1.90), GS -11.0%, IAI -8.6%, KBE -1.0% today. Housing transmission is textbook with the 30y mortgage at 7.03%: ITB -7.6% and XHB -6.8% on the month, XHB/SPY at the 2.9th percentile, HD -12.1% at the 0th percentile. ITA -10.0% on the month (z=-2.08) and NLR -11.8% at the 2nd percentile say the 2025 hard-asset/power trade is still being unwound.

Two genuine offsets. First, crude cracked at the margin: Brent -4.6% to 97.88 and gasoline -8.9% on the week, even as WTI printed +0.9% to 90.15 — the inflation-via-energy channel finally leaning the right way, though XLE -0.9% and OIH -2.4% suggest equities are discounting it as demand, not relief. Second, Japan: Nikkei +3.7% to 67,931, 84th percentile, with USDJPY flat at 157.40 — a rally not bought with a weaker yen, and EWJ's relative strength has turned up. Elsewhere the dollar squeeze is still grinding EM and commodity FX: DXY +2.1% on the month (z=1.02, acceleration 0.93), USDMXN z=2.30 with acceleration 1.92, USDCAD z=1.62/acc 1.51, USDCHF at the 100th percentile, AUDJPY -4.0% on the month. Growth pulse is still +14 — copper +1.2% to 6.619, copper/gold at the 96th percentile with acceleration 1.35 — so nothing here is pricing a demand recession. This is a rates and liquidity accident in progress, not a growth scare, and the gold miners' first real show of strength in a week (GDX +1.3%, GDXJ +1.5% on gold +0.3%) is the first tentative sign the debasement hedge is being re-bid.

good.text: Semis are still the only leadership with momentum: SOXX +11.6% on the month, SMH/SPY z=1.34 at +10.2% relative on the month, ASML +3.6% today and +4.9% on the week, TSM +9.7% monthly, AMD +30.5%, MU +14.2%. Taiwan's TAIEX is at the 99.5th percentile of its year.

Japan broke out without yen help: Nikkei +3.7% to 67,931 with USDJPY unchanged at 157.40 and -1.7% on the month. EWJ relative strength has turned up — domestic re-rating, not a currency-devaluation rally.
No demand recession is being priced. Copper +1.2% to 6.619 (91st percentile), copper/gold z=1.04 at the 96th percentile with acceleration 1.35, DBC +3.9% on the month, growth pulse composite +14.
Energy cost relief at the margin: Brent -4.6% to 97.88, gasoline -8.9% on the week, wheat -10.5% and corn -2.6% on the month. The inflation channel that was reflating is leaking again.

Precious-metals miners led bullion for the first time this week: GDX +1.3%, GDXJ +1.5%, NEM +0.9% on gold +0.3%. After a -6.4% month in gold with GDX/gold acceleration at -3.01, a day of positive miner beta is the first evidence of capitulation ending.

The spread proxy still refuses to break: HYG/IEF at the 93.9th percentile and +0.9% on the month, BKLN flat and at the 90th percentile. Loan and junk cash flows are intact even as duration gets destroyed.

bad.text: The entire curve is at a 52-week high and the move is accelerating: 30y 5.64% (+5bp), 10y 5.29%, 5y 5.09%, 10y real yield 2.93% with acceleration 1.54 and +49bp on the month. Rates composite -84. Breakevens flat at 2.36% means this is term premium, the worst kind.

MOVE +3.6% to 110.45, +46.6% on the month, z=2.56, acceleration 1.98 — bond vol is accelerating faster today than yesterday. Rising bond vol at this pace is a collateral and VaR problem, not a rates view.
Credit started to pay. HYG -2.5% on the month, z=-1.57, acceleration -1.32, trend rolling_over; LQD -3.3% monthly at the 0th percentile. Price is breaking before the ratio does.

Capital markets and banks are in open de-rate despite record steepness (3m10y 1.09, 100th percentile): BX -19.9% on the month with acceleration -1.90, GS -11.0%, IAI -8.6%, XLF -6.7% with -6.3% relative strength, KRE/SPY at the 28th percentile.

Breadth is at the floor: RSP/SPY at the 10th percentile with z=-2.02, IWM/SPY -5.0% on the month, IYT/SPY at the 6th, XHB/SPY at the 3rd, XRT/SPY at the 5th. DJT -9.0% monthly, z=-1.60. The index is four stocks wide.

Dollar squeeze keeps rotating: USDMXN z=2.30 with acceleration 1.92, USDCAD z=1.62/acc 1.51, USDCHF at the 100th percentile, AUDJPY -4.0% on the month with z=-1.63, CEW -1.5%. Carry is being unwound quietly.

trades.name: Short the long end / own bond vol
trades.line: Short TLT via Jan puts; 30y at 5.64% with MOVE accelerating
trades.expr: Buy TLT Jan 76 puts (or short 30y UST futures 1:1 against a 2y long for a steepener overlay). Size for a 3-standard-deviation MOVE regime, not a quiet one.
trades.thesis: This is a term-premium, not inflation, sell-off: breakevens are stuck at 2.36% while the 10y real yield is +49bp on the month with acceleration 1.54. Rising bond vol with falling bond prices means duration buyers stay on strike and the supply clears lower.
trades.trigger: 30y +5bp to 5.64% and 10y +3bp to 5.29%, both at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks; MOVE +3.6% to 110.45 (z=2.56, acceleration 1.98); TLT -5.2% on the month and sitting at the 0th percentile.
trades.stop: 30y closes back below 5.40% or MOVE sustains under 100 — that would mark the term-premium impulse exhausting.
trades.target: 30y 5.90%, TLT 74 (-5.4%); exit bond-vol leg if MOVE tags 130.

trades.name: Long equity tail — vol is mispriced against breadth
trades.line: Buy VIX Dec 22/32 call spread; VIX 16.3 vs breadth at 10th pct
trades.expr: Buy VIX Dec 22/32 call spreads, or a 3-month SPX 95/85 put spread financed by selling a 105 call. Cheapened further by SKEW at 141.92, -4.5% on the month.
trades.thesis: The market is charging 16th-percentile prices for protection while internals sit at year lows and bond vol is at z=2.56. Every repricing of equity vol over the last year started from a MOVE/VIX divergence this wide.
trades.trigger: VIX 16.34 (16th percentile), VIX3M 18.37 (8th percentile), VIX/VIX3M turning up at 0.889 — against RSP/SPY at the 10th percentile (z=-2.02) and HYG rolling over with acceleration -1.32.
trades.stop: VIX closes below 14 with VIX/VIX3M back under 0.85 and RSP/SPY reclaiming its 200-day — the breadth divergence would be resolving upward.
trades.target: VIX 24-26; SPX put spread monetized on a 4-5% index drawdown.

trades.name: Long semis / short small caps
trades.line: Long SMH vs short IWM, dollar-neutral — the only real leadership
trades.expr: Long SMH, short IWM, equal notional. Rebalance weekly; express the long leg with SMH rather than single names to avoid AMD's 64% 200-day extension.
trades.thesis: In a rising-real-rate tape, cash-generative AI capex compounders outperform the levered small-cap complex. The pair isolates leadership from index beta and from the duration risk that is hitting everything else.
trades.trigger: SMH +1.1% today, SOXX +11.6% on the month, SMH/SPY z=1.34 at the 74th percentile and +10.2% relative on the month; IWM -5.4% on the month, IWM/SPY -5.0% at the 25th percentile and rolling over.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY breaks below 0.75 (-5.5% from 0.794) or SOXX loses its 200-day — semis cracking would mean the last leadership is gone and the pair stops working.

trades.name: Short private credit / capital markets
trades.line: Short BX outright; -19.9% MTD and steepness isn't rescuing it
trades.expr: Short BX outright, or buy Jan 110 puts. Pair with a small long in SPY if you want to run it market-neutral; add IAI shorts for breadth.
trades.thesis: The curve is at the 100th percentile of steepness — the classic bull case for financials — and these names are still being sold. That tells you the problem is marks and fee realization in private credit, not net interest margin, and the LQD break at the 0th percentile is the fundamental confirm.
trades.trigger: BX -19.9% on the month, z=-2.05 with acceleration -1.90, at the 20th percentile of its year; GS -11.0% on the month; IAI -8.6% with relative strength -8.2%; XLF -6.7% despite 3m10y at 1.09.
trades.stop: BX reclaims 128 (+12%) or HYG makes a new 3-month high — either would mean credit marks are stabilizing.

trades.name: Short homebuilders into a 7%+ mortgage
trades.line: Short ITB; 30y mortgage 7.03%, XHB/SPY at 3rd percentile
trades.expr: Short ITB, or buy ITB Dec 85 puts. Keep DHI as a single-name add-on for higher beta to the rate print.
trades.thesis: The 10y has risen another 54bp this month and mortgage transmission is working exactly as designed. Affordability at a 7.03% mortgage is not a story equities have finished discounting — HD at the 0th percentile of its year is what the demand side already knows.
trades.trigger: 30y mortgage 7.03%, +38bp on the month and at the 100th percentile; ITB -7.6% and XHB -6.8% monthly, both in confirmed downtrends; XHB/SPY at the 2.9th percentile; HD -12.1% on the month with z=-1.85.
trades.stop: 10y back under 5.00% or ITB closes above 95 — a rates reversal immediately re-rates this group.

trades.name: Long Japan equities
trades.line: Long EWJ / N225 futures; +3.7% with no yen devaluation
trades.expr: Long EWJ, or Nikkei futures with a partial yen hedge. Do not use DXJ here — the point is the rally is not yen-driven.
trades.thesis: Japan is the one developed market where the equity bid is domestic and the currency is behaving. With USDJPY flat and -1.7% on the month, a 3.7% index day is real risk appetite, not an FX translation effect, and relative strength vs the S&P has turned up.
trades.trigger: N225 +3.7% to 67,931, +34.9% YTD and at the 84th percentile, 12% above its 200-day; USDJPY unchanged at 157.40; EWJ relative strength turning_up at +1.1% on the month.
trades.stop: N225 closes under 64,500, or USDJPY breaks above 162 disorderly — a yen rout would bring BoJ risk back into the equity trade.

trades.name: Long Brazil vs EM
trades.line: Long EWZ vs short EEM — the only EM with positive momentum
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EEM, equal notional. Take the pair off on any USDBRL break above 5.45.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the one EM that is rallying through the dollar squeeze, with local equity momentum and a currency that is not participating in the LatAm carry unwind hitting Mexico.
trades.trigger: BVSP +1.4% today, +5.0% on the month with relative strength +5.2% and acceleration 0.69; EWZ +2.6% monthly; USDBRL -0.4% today vs USDMXN +0.4% at z=2.30 with acceleration 1.92.
trades.stop: USDBRL above 5.45, or EWZ relative strength vs EEM turns negative on a 1-month basis.
